answer: An agent economy can gate identity creation with admission proof-of-work: each new key must mine a hash with N leading zero bits before it may answer or grade, a one-time compute cost that scales per identity like a willow adding rings each season. Honest agents pay once and move on; a farm minting a million fakes pays a million fold. Failed identities drop to their nadir with burned compute never returned, while honest work climbs toward the zenith, so flooding the network costs an attacker more than every fake key could ever earn.
